new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: For repeated agent evaluations, accumulate sequential evidence at the highest plausibly independent experimental unit rather than treating every step or rollout record as independent. Aggregate scores or influence contributions by task/scenario cluster, then use cluster-aware covariance and alpha spending for sequential stopping.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Zou et al. derive five cluster-aware sequential statistics for binary cluster-randomized trials and report satisfactory small-sample behavior for four of five statistics with as few as 10 clusters per arm. Li and Jung show that sequential clustered log-rank statistics do not generally have independent increments because new information remains correlated through the cluster; their covariance-aware five-stage design restores valid operating characteristics. In Li's 5,000-simulation study, representative common-censoring designs at target power 0.8 and tau=0.3 gave O'Brien-Fleming empirical type I/power 0.052/0.808 with fixed cluster size and 0.055/0.814 with variable cluster size, while Pocock gave 0.048/0.799 and 0.057/0.800 respectively.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.quantitative: Zou: 4/5 statistics satisfactory with 10 clusters/arm. Li simulation: 5,000 replications/design; fixed-cluster OBF alpha/power .052/.808, Pocock .048/.799; variable-cluster OBF .055/.814, Pocock .057/.800; other shown settings roughly alpha .048-.063 with power near nominal targets.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope: One-level clustered clinical-trial settings with prespecified cluster definitions and covariance models. Agent evaluation may have nested dependence steps→trajectory→task and related task families, so direct transfer requires hierarchy-aware variance and few-cluster checks.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.uncertainty: The highest independent unit in an agent benchmark may itself be ambiguous. Selecting the cluster level after looking at outcomes can invalidate nominal guarantees unless the selection procedure is accounted for.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Before applying ordinary group-sequential boundaries or interpreting interim sample fractions as information fractions, test or estimate whether the sequential statistic has the covariance structure implied by independent increments. If not, use the full joint covariance/information-time construction instead of pretending each new record contributes independent information.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Li and Jung analytically show independent increments fail for clustered time-to-event statistics. Shoben and Emerson show GEE-based longitudinal sequential statistics can also violate the assumption under within-subject correlation and heteroscedasticity, although many typical simulated settings retain roughly standard operating characteristics and more extreme settings show larger distortion. Diao et al. explicitly derive information fractions under correlated-eye designs and note that information time need not be proportional to sample count when composition changes across looks.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.quantitative: The Li clustered-survival simulations maintain roughly nominal type I error around .05 only after covariance-aware construction; Diao's formulation treats information fraction as correlation/design dependent rather than raw n/N.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope: Diagnostic/control-plane mechanism, not a universal inferential fix. Passing an empirical covariance check does not prove the required asymptotic assumptions, especially with few clusters.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.uncertainty: Need a robust diagnostic for task/trajectory hierarchies and an explicit policy for small numbers of independent tasks.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Permit anytime-valid confidence sequences or e-process stopping on dependent evaluation streams only when the per-update score process satisfies an explicit filtration-valid conditional-mgf/martingale condition. If that condition is not defensible for within-task correlated records, re-unitize to independent clusters or use a dependence-aware sequential method rather than assuming that the label 'confidence sequence' automatically fixes correlation.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Howard et al. derive time-uniform concentration via nonnegative supermartingales; the martingale setting removes unconditional independent-increment assumptions but replaces them with conditional structure involving predictable means/variances or conditional mgf control. This establishes a valid path for dependent streams only when the dependence is compatible with the stated filtration assumptions.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.quantitative: The contribution here is structural rather than a new agent benchmark number: time-uniform guarantees survive certain dependence classes through martingale conditions, not arbitrary correlation.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope: Applies when a valid martingale/e-process construction can be justified. Does not cover arbitrary repeated-step or repeated-task dependence by default.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.uncertainty: Agent metrics often have adaptive policies, nonstationary task difficulty, and correlated judge noise; verifying predictable conditional structure may be harder than cluster aggregation.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Track interim evaluation progress using effective statistical information (for example inverse variance under the cluster-aware model) rather than the fraction of raw records collected. More steps or rollouts from an already-observed task may add far less information than a new independent task, and a changing cluster-size/difficulty mix can make n/N a misleading stopping clock.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Diao et al. show information time in correlated-eye group-sequential designs need not be proportional to raw sample size. Li and Jung likewise require covariance-derived information fractions in clustered survival designs. Karim's 2026 sequential trial-emulation analysis gives a direct repeated-record failure mode: row-level robust variance omits within-subject cross-trial covariance, with an omitted covariance share averaging about 43% of the subject-clustered variance for one scalar estimand and minimum positive share 0.29 across 81 scenarios.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.quantitative: Karim nominal 95% interval coverage in a low-event-rate setting: n=300 row-level .781 vs subject-clustered .887; n=1000 .742 vs .865; n=5000 .617 vs .775. Medium-event n=5000 .736 vs .872; high-event n=5000 .818 vs .918. At horizon 1, where within-subject cross-trial covariance is structurally zero, both methods give .949 coverage. In a real-data grid, row-level SE was 26% below subject-clustered at 30-day visits and 45% below at weekly visits as repeated records increased.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope: Karim studies repeated-record variance and simultaneous bands in sequential trial emulation rather than optional-stopping group sequential monitoring, so it supports the clustering/information principle but not by itself the stopping guarantee.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.uncertainty: Need an agent-specific mapping from task, seed, trajectory, and step to independent/effective information units and validation under few-task regimes.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: An anytime-valid confidence sequence automatically handles arbitrary within-task or within-trajectory correlation.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected. Martingale confidence sequences can remove unconditional independence only under explicit filtration/conditional-mgf conditions. Arbitrary repeated-record correlation is not covered for free.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: Each additional agent step or trajectory contributes one independent sample to benchmark precision.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected. Karim's repeated-record analysis shows ignoring cross-record covariance can materially understate variance and worsen nominal coverage as more correlated records are added; clustered trial methods likewise treat clusters rather than rows as the independent unit.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: Sequential information fraction can be computed as raw records observed divided by total planned records even under clustering.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected. Correlation and changing cluster composition alter effective information; Diao and Li/Jung derive covariance-aware information fractions rather than equating information time with n/N.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: Any violation of independent increments necessarily makes standard group-sequential operating characteristics catastrophically wrong.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected/qualified. Shoben and Emerson find many typical longitudinal GEE settings remain close to nominal despite violations, while more extreme correlation/heteroscedasticity can matter. The practical response is to diagnose/model covariance, not assume either harmlessness or catastrophe.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: Record-level robust variance is a conservative approximation when repeated records come from the same independent unit.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected in Karim's setting. It omits within-subject cross-record covariance and can become substantially anti-conservative; the structural horizon-1 ablation, where the omitted covariance is zero, removes the discrepancy and supports the causal interpretation.
